comparator.name: Bachelor Bestuurskunde
comparator.sourceNotes: Recovered from the verified existing canonical record; no root production decision existed at recovery. Current 2026–2027 ESSB EER Appendix III B (p.38) confirms all 22 components and 60+60+60 EC for Dutch Bestuurskunde. Do not substitute MISOC, whose adjacent English-language table has different components. Articles 3.3–3.6 and 4.1–4.2 verify instruction/assessment, approved 15-EC minor, progression and 135-EC thesis entry. First enrolment in Bachelor-3 excludes the autumn thesis round. The public overview supplies the ten-week second-year internship, skill and research context. Retained all original external credits and both UCR course selections/schedules. The missing decision is a provenance/replay repair, not evidence that previous selection was independently compiled. Original rationale and full canonical snapshot are preserved in the case evidence.

selection.assessment: Two alternatives are included. The closest match is retained. A second, evidence-backed climate and sustainability governance route differs by seven courses / 52.5 EC. The previously proposed law/institutions and public-organisation routes are not retained because they did not clear the 30 EC / four-course distinctness floor without arbitrary substitutions. All 15 generator-eligible rows are assessed substantively. The closest concept owns public-problem analysis (318,322), governance (319), policy (320), public organisations (321), politics/law/sociology/economics (323–326), independent research skills with an explicit required-thesis gap (341), and divergent public interests (342). Housing (328), crime (329) and insecure work (330) are public-problem applications of that core, not claims of housing, criminology or labour-economics specialisations. The second concept is generated by the explicit climate-policy signal (327). Law and organisation are genuine defining components of the closest response, not separate residual candidates. A legal/public-organisation reweighting does not establish four content-justified changes as a separate programme here. A dedicated housing-planning direction is not established by the available catalogue: Spatial Planning has no offered term. Public Policy Analysis likewise has no offered term in 2026–2029, so it is not inserted to fill policy gaps. Additional criminal-justice or psychological interests are not inferred from individual alumni security trajectories. Two strong responses are retained; this is not a claim that every other conceivable combination is impossible.

alternatives.label: Closest match to Bestuurskunde
alternatives.labelReason: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and accurately presents this option as the closest feasible UCR response to Bachelor Bestuurskunde, rather than as a narrower subfield.
alternatives.concept: Politics, law, sociology and economics provide different ways to examine public institutions and policy choices. Research methods, ethics, organizational psychology and leadership connect those perspectives to public problems. This is an interdisciplinary UCR response, with gaps in dedicated public-administration teaching and compulsory professional practice.
progression: Passed after re-sequencing the sociology strand so Introduction to Sociology precedes Modern Sociology, which in turn precedes New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory. Formal prerequisites and fixed-term availability remain satisfied. Independently rechecked against the current enriched workbook: all formal prerequisites are satisfied strictly earlier and every scheduled term is offered. Advanced international/governance courses without formal prerequisites follow comparative-politics foundations. R3 follows Sustainability Essentials II; sustainability governance has no formal prerequisite and draws on first-semester social/political foundations.

alternatives.label: Climate & sustainability governance
alternatives.labelReason: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and describes its substantive organising direction without treating the generating concept as an official UCR track or overstating one strand of the programme.
alternatives.concept: Public institutions and policy are studied alongside climate change, water management, environmental justice and resource stewardship. Science and laboratory study support informed analysis of sustainability choices. The programme combines governance with environmental knowledge; it is not a specialist public-administration or environmental-engineering degree.
progression: Passed after replacing the advanced contemporary-social-theory course with Modern Sociology, so Introduction to Sociology precedes the later sociology course; Sustainability Essentials I also precedes Sustainability Essentials II. Formal prerequisites and fixed-term availability remain satisfied. Independently rechecked against the current enriched workbook: all formal prerequisites are satisfied strictly earlier and every scheduled term is offered. Advanced international/governance courses without formal prerequisites follow comparative-politics foundations. R3 follows Sustainability Essentials II; sustainability governance has no formal prerequisite and draws on first-semester social/political foundations.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces seven courses (52.5 EC) with sustainability and environmental-governance study. The changed courses are consequences of the evidenced climate-policy direction, not threshold-filling substitutions.

blocks: UCR examines states, institutions, democracies, regimes and political explanation using empirical political science. This supports a subject-level relationship to EUR Political Science, without certifying identical topics or depth.

UCR explicitly studies rule-making and collective decision-making involving governmental and non-governmental actors, policy enforcement and competing interests. The EUR overview and ministry-internship account identify network governance as an applied institutional subject. Shared governance content supports a partial relationship; UCR is sustainability-focused, not the complete EUR network-governance syllabus.

UCR teaches EU actors, institutions, decision rules, interest groups and legislative research. This is a substantive European-governance relationship; the broader international coverage of the EUR component is not wholly reproduced.

UCR profile explicitly covers constitutional AND administrative law and compares five legal systems. This is a substantive partial relationship to the EUR state/administrative-law component, not equivalent Dutch public-law training.

UCR studies political authority, institutional organization and normative/empirical political problems through major thinkers. This supports political-philosophy correspondence; coverage of democracy and specific authors may differ.
No scheduled course introduces Public Administration as a full disciplinary framework. Politics, sociology and law are concrete complementary strands, not a substitute for this subject.
No scheduled course reproduces the general public-policy component. Available sustainability governance is focused on environmental cases; Public Policy Analysis in the catalogue has no offered term.
Econometrics, ethics and economics can inform policy inquiry but do not constitute the dedicated policy-analysis component. GOSPOLI312 has no scheduled availability.
Several courses address institutions and society, but none is verified as a sufficiently direct counterpart to this integrated EUR component.

UCR teaches motivation, groups, culture, structure and organizational change. This is a concrete organizational-behaviour relationship to EUR Organisation & Management; public-sector and general-management coverage differ.

UCR teaches market structure, consumer/firm behaviour and macroeconomic conditions. This supplies introductory economic reasoning relevant to EUR Economics, Welfare & Distribution; no claim that UCR introductory economics duplicates all welfare/distribution teaching.

UCR Public Economics studies taxation, public spending, redistribution, public goods and government intervention. These directly support analysis of public-resource allocation; managerial/budget-practice dimensions of the EUR subject are not certified equivalent.
UCR teaches inclusive leadership, diversity, ethical teams and collaborative practice. These form a concrete partial people-management relationship; it is not a dedicated public-sector HR curriculum.

Shared introductory sociological concepts, institutions and social structure; UCR profile explicitly includes major theorists and research perspectives. EUR Appendix III and intended outcomes establish the sociology foundation; full syllabus equivalence is not asserted.

UCR teaches operationalization, sampling, research design and group research. These are concrete social-research-design skills corresponding to EUR Designing Social Research and its formal research outcomes; the statistical component is additional.

UCR explicitly teaches qualitative design, collection, management, interpretation, reflexivity and dissemination. This supports the dedicated qualitative-research component and formal EUR research competency, without claiming identical methods exercises.

UCR Econometrics teaches OLS/GLS/IV estimation, hypothesis tests, Stata simulations and an empirical paper. This is concrete quantitative-analysis overlap with EUR Quantitative Methods and the formal quantitative-research outcome, not a claim of identical statistical coverage or an entire social-methods sequence.
Research skills and group assignments do not by themselves establish the EUR dedicated 7.5-EC Research Project; preserve a deliberate gap.
No scheduled course is a required 15-EC public-administration bachelor project. Optional UCR independent research is separate from the 180 EC and is not a compulsory substitute.

The EUR overview specifies reading scientific articles, literature-study writing and research presentation. UCR PPD explicitly develops source analysis, research questions, writing/speaking, collaboration and reflective learning. Their academic-skills function substantially corresponds, with distinct delivery.
The required EUR 15-EC public-sector internship and ten-week placement are not replaced by a taught UCR course.
The 15-EC approved minor has no specified subject here, so no taught UCR subject is invented as an equivalent.

notes.text: EUR combines public-administration theory and policy analysis with law, economics, sociology, management, a required public-sector internship and a bachelor project. UCR offers related interdisciplinary study, with a second option focused on sustainability governance. It does not reproduce the dedicated policy, internship and bachelor-project sequence. Shared rows include partial content relationships; blank cells show deliberate gaps. Optional independent research is additional to the displayed 180 EC.

audience.programmeDescription: Public Administration (Bestuurskunde) at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how governments and public organizations address social problems. Students combine policy, politics, law, sociology, economics and management with social research, a public-sector internship and a bachelor project. The selected programme is the Dutch-language full-time bachelor.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR option combines the main neighbouring disciplines; the second adds a substantial climate and sustainability focus. Neither reproduces EUR’s dedicated public-administration degree. In particular, general public policy, policy analysis, the required internship and the bachelor-project sequence remain important differences. Shared rows show content relationships, including partial matches, rather than course equivalence.

curriculum.limitation: The complete EUR curriculum comprises 180 EC over three years, including a 15-EC approved minor. Some lectures are in English; the Dutch offering retains Dutch working groups, assignments and assessments.
